analysis.title: Amer Sports Inc. (AS): 3Q26 First Take: Broad-based beat and FY26 raise; initial FY27 outlook calls for continued growth and margin
key_insights: AS reported adjusted 3Q26 EPS of $0.42 vs GS/FactSet consensus of $0.34/$0.35. Revenue rose 23.5% Y/Y to $2.17bn vs GS/consensus of +22.2%/+21.6%, with double-digit growth across all segments, geographies and channels.
Adjusted gross margin expanded 150bps Y/Y to 59.4% vs GS/consensus of 59.0%/59.2%. Adjusted operating margin was 16.4% vs GS/consensus of 14.1%/14.5%.
Growth engines: Arc'teryx omni-comp +16%, Salomon Softgoods strong momentum, Wilson Tennis 360 continued growth.

FY26 guidance raised: adj. EPS $1.32-$1.35 (prior $1.27-$1.30) vs GS/consensus $1.32/$1.31. Revenue growth 25%-26% including ~200bps FX benefit (prior ~24% including 200-250bps FX) vs GS/consensus +24.9%/+25.0%.
FY26 adjusted operating margin guided to 14.5%-14.7% (prior 14.2%-14.5%), implying ~140bps expansion at midpoint vs GS/consensus of 120bps/130bps.

Segment FY26 guidance: Technical Apparel revenue +27%-28% (prior 25%-26%), margin 23.0%-23.2% (prior ~22.5%). Outdoor Performance revenue +28%-29% (prior 27%-28%), margin 17.0%-17.2% (prior 16.0%-16.5%). Ball & Racquet revenue +14%-15% (prior ~14%), margin ~6% (prior 6.7%-7.2%).

Initial FY27 framework: revenue growth at the midpoint of the long-term algorithm of low-double-digit to mid-teens, and adjusted operating margin expansion at the low end of the 30-70+ bps annual algorithm.
New open-ended $1bn buyback authorization, with up to $200mn expected to be repurchased by year-end 2026.
GS notes management indicated momentum has continued into 4Q, but the guidance raise was smaller than the 3Q beat.
GS focus areas: durability of elevated growth as Arc'teryx and Salomon cycle tougher comparisons, FY27 building blocks, balance of reinvestment vs margin expansion, and capital allocation.
Regional revenue growth Y/Y: Americas +22.2% to $702mn, EMEA +10.2% to $582mn, Greater China +30.4% to $602mn, APAC ex-China +47.6% to $284mn. DTC +36.0%, wholesale +14.8%.

Technical Apparel sales +26.0% Y/Y (24% ex-FX), adjusted operating margin 21.1% (+210bps). Outdoor Performance sales +26.7% Y/Y (26% ex-FX), omni-comp +28%, adjusted operating margin 23.1% (+80bps). Ball & Racquet sales +12.0% Y/Y, adjusted operating margin 6.1% (-210bps), below GS at 8.2% but above consensus at 4.8%.
Adjusted SG&A was 43.1% of sales ($934.8mn). Adjusted EBITDA margin 21.5% vs GS/consensus 18.9%/19.6%. Inventory +15.5% Y/Y to $1.98bn, below GS forecast of +17.4%.
The FY26 outlook assumes the most recently announced Section 301 tariff rates remain in place through the rest of 2026.

market_movers.rationale: Buy with a $43 12-month target based on 14.0x Q5-Q8 EV/EBITDA, implying 47.8% upside from $29.10. GS calls the 3Q result another solid print with a broad-based beat and a raise that extends beyond revenue.

risk_factors: Slower than anticipated growth in Greater China.
Weaker brand momentum due to slower innovation.
Corporate structure, including Cayman Islands incorporation and shifts in support from several majority shareholders.
Lower real estate availability or quality.
Arc'teryx and Salomon cycling increasingly difficult comparisons may slow growth.
geopolitical: The FY26 outlook assumes the most recently announced Section 301 tariff rates remain in place for the rest of 2026.

tension_points.bull_case: Broad-based double-digit growth across segments, regions and channels, a FY26 raise extending to margin and EPS, momentum continuing into 4Q, and a new $1bn buyback.
tension_points.bear_case: Arc'teryx and Salomon cycle increasingly difficult comparisons, and the guidance raise was smaller than the 3Q beat.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Slowing Arc'teryx omni-comp or weaker 4Q commentary and FY27 building blocks on the conference call, with growth falling below the low-double-digit end of the long-term algorithm.

theme_stances.key_argument: The 3Q beat was broad-based and the FY26 raise extends beyond revenue to operating margin and EPS.
